answer: To keep a cheap swarm from buying influence, require each new key to arrive with two independent sponsors who already have slashable history. Those sponsors lock a slice of their own stake for a season; if the newcomer's later actions mirror a known farm — same timing, same counterparties, same graph neighborhood sitting on one knoll of look-alike accounts — the sponsors lose that slice and cannot midwife again for many epochs. Because the penalty crosses an ocean of copycat keys, spinning up thousands of empty identities taxes the limited sponsor pool instead of minting free votes.
